node.text: We are here to plumb the depths of deep time. I am charged by the Chief Executor of Archaeology herself to lead this expedition. While our Artifices are the greatest in all the world, our forebears were possessed of even greater powers of creation. And so we seek out their works, and more importantly their workplaces, so that we might learn their secrets.
node.choice: I see, thank you. Let us return to my other questions.
Might I be able to assist in this endeavour?
Live and drink.

node.text: Surely, you have not forgotten your own people? The glorious towers of the executorial estates? The great forges of the Artifices? The indomitable praetorian legion? A jest, it must be. Well nonetheless, I am sure you know our ways. Our ceaseless ambition to improve our metrics of key performance, our ambition to reclaim the mantle of our forebears and surpass even their lofty heights.

Why of course, it is my duty to inform the world of the opportunities our great home might afford them. We are an ancient people, and our home is far to the north, across the wretched Salt Desert, through the mountains, and across the frozen plain of Arthax. Deep beneath the ground, our home uses the warmth of the earth to power our great machines, farms, forges and automatons. Our legions protect us, and our Artifices create greater and greater works of technology, that we might one day surpass even our forebears. I encourage you to speak with our merchant, who I am certain will have wares of interest to you.

No doubt were they to be successful, they would eventually turn on my people and the other clans, before turning inwards and devouring themselves.
They hail from the mountains of the north, far to the east of our home. I suggest caution when dealing with them. Avoid them if possible, and if this proves impossible: be prepared for battle at any moment.

node.text: Hailing far from the south, I know little of these people, other than their fearsome reputation. It is said that they have great command over the toxic flora of their homeland, and dark rumours suround their religious practices. Some say they believe that the sun only rises thanks to a nightly blood sacrifice, and they conduct vicious hunts through their lands and beyond to ensure, from their perspective, that the sun always rises again.

node.text: We have conducted much trade with this people. An archipelago far to the west is their home. They are prolific miners and sailors, carving their great halls beneath the earth, and their towers above it, while trading all across the known world. Worthy allies, should you be so lucky as to meet them.

node.text:
My scouts report that the ancient ruins of Qud are somewhat divided, in the danger and value of the treasure to be found. Further east, on the shores of the great reef, there are areas known as baroque ruins. We have found inteligence that one ruin in particular resides there, and I greatly wish to establish a second base there.
Of the scouts I sent, only one returned, and they did not survive their injuries. Before their passing, the scout spoke of a dangerous journey through the black jungles of deep Qud, and the ruin itself was populated by no small number of extremely hostile creatures.
My request then, is that you travel to this ruin, and drive out anything that might represent a threat to us. What say you?

node.text: Surely, you have not forgotten your own people? Perhaps an unfortunate meeting with the vile mind sucking winged rodents or leeches that seem to infest this land of screams? It seems you are due to pilgrimage down the Null River to the jungles of our home. To see again the Black Ziggurats of the Valley of the Archpriests. To feel the thrill of Her grace as you prowl the Arboreta and His balm as you repose in the shade of the valley. Speak with the trader, perhaps some of their wares will invoke a memory of home.

Few outsiders have ever reached the Arboreta,and fewer still have returned to tell of it, so your curiosity is only natural. Far to the southeast, the Null River, stalked by the Mindrend Ibis and other such creatures, weaves through the desert. Some distance along it's length, the great jungles tended by our horticulturalists rise. The air is thick with toxins, and at night all manner of predators stalk it's shade. Deep within these jungles are the great Ziggurats of the Valley of the Archpriests, and it is here that my people are at home.
At every Jeweled dusk, when the respective masters of the cycle trade positions, the day's sacrifice is offered to the Syzgy that His warmth might return to us.

node.text: Stop hunting? That will not do. The goatfolk are the most numerous and easily hunted of the jungle. And we cannot be without sacrifices. So it is as I always believed- you must kill them and free me by force.

choice.text: For the love your people bear me, I ask you- do me this favour and allow me to save your life without further bloodshed.

node.choice: The goatfolk take many prisoners themselves. What if they offered to trade those that they capture to you instead?
I am not yet convinced a peaceful option is impossible. Live and drink.
I see, Live and drink.

node.text: Accept tribute from these savages? An interesting suggestion. As long as the blood flows, He is rejuvenated. And we have much in the way of trade. Very well. Suggest this solution to the savage chief, and report back to me.
node.choice: I will return with news.

node.text: An interesting proposition. I accept. The finer details can be worked out in the future, but in the meantime, I assume you have arranged for my freedom?

choice.text: I have indeed. In return for sacrifices from the jungle, the goatfolk will accept peace with the Ekuemekiyye. I have been given permission to free you.

node.choice: I must speak to the chieftain again, Live and drink.

node.text: By Her grace, it is about time. If I see another savage I will have no choice but to slay it. I will return to the encampment shortly. You may see the Priest of All Suns there for your reward.
